messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: NCCL watchdog triggered on cluster inference-pool-2 (priority=P1) — multiple tp jobs hung, repeated NCCL timeouts and container restarts. Paging #oncall-tp
ops-bot: auto-bridging to #incidents and creating conference bridge (zoom.me/xxxx)
oncall-tp: I'm on it. Joining bridge. Can someone drop initial symptoms?
sara: saw spike in `tp4` jobs started at 2026-03-15T02:22Z, then ~02:24 we see repeated `NCCL timeout` on two pods across nodes gpu-12 and gpu-15. Pods restarted 3x each.
mike: adding logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-15 02:24:11] NCCL WARN NetService: timeout waiting for 192.168.10.15:51820
[2026-03-15 02:24:11] NCCL ERROR Unhandled timeout during allreduce
[2026-03-15 02:24:11] CUDA ERROR Xid 46: GPU page fault, killing context
```
cheng: Xid 46 repeated ~14 times across the run on both nodes; kernel shows `GPU page fault` not a simple OOM. Also `nvidia-smi` on g1 shows ECC errors rising.
devon: Confirmed container restarts had exit code 137 sometimes and also OOM -> but some were kernel kill due to Xid 46. Looks like memory corruption on the NIC path?
oncall-tp: I'm going to temporarily remove new tp4 rollout from the LB and shift traffic to stable-replica. Doing `kubectl scale` now.
sara: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy tp4-workers --replicas=0` executed at 3181234590
mike: Routing change done; API traffic routed to `rwd-quant-v2` and `rwd-onthefly` fallbacks. Noting increased p99 latency for some customers ~2.3x during reroute.
support-lia: Support: impact: ~4 paying customers showed errors (500) and queued requests. Triage lists: tenant ids t-9912, t-2341, t-7745. Notified accounts team.
pm-anna: Any ETA? Customers asking for root cause and mitigation steps.
oncall-tp: Running `kubectl exec -n kube-system -it nccl-watchdog -- tail -n 200 /var/log/nccl.log` and collecting `dmesg` from nodes. Also checking `ibstat` and `mlxconfig`.
devon: here's useful command set I ran: ```sh
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide -l job=tp4
kubectl logs -n inference tp4-worker-7 -c runner --since=10m
ssh ubuntu@gpu-12 'dmesg | tail -n 80'
```
mike: dmesg excerpt: ```
[Mar 15 02:23:59] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 46, GPU fault at 0x12345
[Mar 15 02:24:01] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0:  device fault state 0x1
```
cheng: mlx5 device faults + GPU page faults -> suggests a fabric/driver interaction. Could be firmware or MLX driver regression. Are we on a recent driver?
sara: nodes gpu-12 and gpu-15 are on nvidia-driver 530.71.13 and mlx5 firmware 23.4. We had a driver roll 3 days ago for perf.
oncall-tp: Rolling back driver on gpu-15 to previous vendor snapshot `530.67.01` for test. Will drain and reboot node.
devon: Suggested mitigation: cordon + drain, evict pods, reboot NIC + GPU, then reintroduce node. Also propose increasing NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME and NCCL param tuning as temporary stopgap: `NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0`, `NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=2`, and bump `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1`.
mike: Applied cordon: `kubectl cordon gke-gpu-15` at 3181234620. Started `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gke-gpu-15`
ops-bot: Notice: new ephemeral fallback created: `tp-shared-fallback-quant` to pick up queued jobs.
sara: After reboot of gpu-15, early signs: no Xid 46 for ~3m but still seeing two NCCL timeouts on gpu-12. Planning to reboot gpu-12 next.
oncall-tp: Eng infra, can we pause any non-critical background jobs on the cluster controlling link utilization? Maybe some heavy backup traffic or training runs are coinciding.
cheng: Checked cluster net metrics: IB retransmits spiked during window 02:23-02:26 by ~12x. Could be transient congestion, but device faults point to driver/firmware interplay.
devon: We're enabling automatic fallback for multi-GPU jobs: set routing policy `prefer_single_gpu=true` for affected customers for next 2 hours via console.
sara: Support asked: what's ETA for restoring full multi-GPU? We can bring nodes back after firmware rollback+reboot validation ~30-45m.
mike: Running heal checklist: 1) cordon g12/g15 2) drain 3) reboot nodes 4) rollback driver to 530.67.01 5) monitor `dmesg` / `nccl` logs for 10m 6) uncordon if clean.
oncall-tp: I'm assigning followups: @cheng driver/firmware lead to investigate recent roll 3 days ago; @devon routing config to keep single-GPU fallbacks until 03:30Z; @sara collect full logs & tenant impact; @mike coordinate reboots.
pm-anna: I'll prepare customer comms draft: short outage note, mitigation steps, and ETA.
support-lia: Notified affected customers with an interim message. Will update per 15-min cadence.
ops-bot: Incident timeline updated in incident tracker: https://redwood.incidents/IR-2026-73
sara: Post-reboot gpu-15 logs: `no further Xid 46`, mlx5 errors reduced, IB retransmits down to baseline. Promoting node back to pool now.
mike: Uncordoned gke-gpu-15 at 3181234680. Running small tp4 smoke job to validate interconnect.
oncall-tp: Smoke looks good, allreduce completed within expected latency. Reintroducing multi-GPU traffic gradually with canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%.
sara: Canary at 50% for 12 mins, no new NCCL errors. Rolling to 100%.
support-lia: Customers reporting improved behavior, errors cleared.
pm-anna: Will follow up with RCA: suspected recent driver/firmware combo + transient IB congestion causing GPU page faults (Xid 46) -> NCCL timeouts -> container restarts. Next steps: block rolling driver until deeper validation, add net retransmit alerts, and add NCCL ASYNC error handling in runtime configs.
oncall-tp: Closing pager for now. Leaving this thread open for notes and RCA drafts. :white_check_mark:
